facts.text: Milford is a village in Oakland County, located within Milford Township.

Downtown Milford serves as the local downtown for residents of both the village and Milford Township, as well as surrounding communities, with a walkable streetscape of shops, restaurants and professional services.

The North Milford Village Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000, takes in the commercial area along Main Street from the Huron River to Summit, industrial areas around the mill ponds west of Main, and residential areas east of Main.
Houses in the historic district span many styles, including Greek Revival, Italianate, Queen Anne, Craftsman and Bungalow.
Central Park is a 12-acre park in the heart of the community, within easy walking distance of downtown, with the Huron River and Pettibone Creek as its backdrop.
Milford began with a sawmill, its Lower and Upper Mill Ponds were created in 1836 and 1845 to power mills and factories, and hydropower gave the village electric lights in 1892.
Hubbell Pond Park is the site of the YMCA, the library and a trail system that runs from Commerce Road to Kensington Park on South Milford Road.

On the Thursday before Thanksgiving, Main Street businesses wrap their window displays like Christmas presents, and at 6:30 p.m. children tear the wrap away to reveal decorated holiday displays at The Big Reveal.
Downtown Milford's Christmas Parade is held on the Saturday after Thanksgiving at 10 a.m.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Milford, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation for Milford homes, from Queen Anne gables to Bungalow porches. Designed, hung, serviced and taken down. Free estimates.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Milford, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Rooflines, porches and trees lit in clean, even lines, then serviced through the season and taken down after the holidays. Free estimates in the village and Milford Township.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: The North Milford Village Historic District takes in Greek Revival, Italianate, Queen Anne, Craftsman and Bungalow houses, and each style asks something different of a lighting plan. A Queen Anne may have layered gables and a wide porch worth tracing. An Italianate's deep, bracketed eaves reward one crisp line. A Bungalow's low roof brings the porch and front shrubs to eye level, so the display should start there. We design around the house you actually have, not a template. Crews reach the high peaks from a bucket truck where the lot allows and hang every run by hand. Then we service the display through the season and take it all down after the holidays.
considerations: Historic houses often keep original wood trim, gutters and porch details. We decide how each run attaches with the age and condition of those surfaces in mind, and we want to hear about anything fragile before install day. Some trim is better left unlit, and we will say so.

If your yard has a tall maple, an old oak or a row of evergreens, lighting it can extend the display well past the roofline. Wraps on trunks and limbs take height and time, so we plan them from the bucket truck and space the lights to read clearly from the street.

Older homes can have few exterior outlets, sometimes sharing a circuit with rooms inside. During the estimate we find every usable outlet and plan the layout around them. If a design needs more power than the house has, you hear about it before installation, not halfway through.
faq: Do you install Christmas lights in Milford?

Yes. The Village of Milford and the surrounding Milford Township are both inside our Southeast Michigan service area. Call (248) 756-8915 or send the request form with your address, and we will set up a free estimate.
Does a historic house change how the lights go up?

It can. Original trim, older roofing and decorative porch work call for a careful plan. We look at each surface during the estimate, decide how the runs will attach, and point out any spot where we would rather not hang lights at all.
When should I book to have lights up by the Christmas Parade?

Early. Downtown Milford's Christmas Parade falls on the Saturday after Thanksgiving, and residential installs commonly run from October into early December. A request in September or October gives you the widest choice of dates, and your install date is set with you when you book.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Milford, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Storefront and window lighting for downtown Milford shops, restaurants and offices. Walkthrough, design, install, service and removal from one company.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Milford, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Window framing, doorways, storefront trees and building outlines for Main Street shops, restaurants and offices. One plan and one contact from walkthrough to removal.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Milford is where the village, Milford Township and nearby communities come for shops, restaurants and professional services, and it is built for walking. That changes how commercial lighting should work. People see your building from the sidewalk, close enough to notice every window frame, doorway and planter tree, so the details matter as much as the roofline. The season also starts early on Main Street. Decorated windows are unwrapped at The Big Reveal on the Thursday before Thanksgiving, and the Christmas Parade follows on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. A display that is already lit by then makes the most of those days downtown. From the walkthrough to removal after the season, one company handles the design, the bucket-truck install and every service call in between.
considerations: On a walkable street, the details up close carry the display. Framed windows and doors, a wrapped planter tree, or bistro lights over outdoor seating give passersby something to notice before they reach your door, and they photograph well at night.

The Big Reveal and the Christmas Parade are fixed points on Milford's holiday calendar. Tell us at the walkthrough which dates matter to your business, and we will plan the install schedule with them in mind, along with your hours and deliveries.

Main Street's commercial area from the Huron River to Summit sits inside the North Milford Village Historic District. On an older storefront, the walkthrough looks closely at the facade and original trim before any attachment point is chosen, and it also covers the power supply and where a bucket truck can park.
faq: Do you work with businesses in downtown Milford?

Yes. Milford is inside our service area, and we light storefronts, restaurants, offices and multi-tenant buildings. Commercial projects begin with a free walkthrough to look at the building, the power and lift access, followed by a written estimate.
How early should we book for The Big Reveal?

As early as you can. Commercial displays take more planning than homes, and walkthroughs in late summer or early fall leave the most room on the schedule before the Thursday before Thanksgiving. A later request still gets a straight answer about what the schedule allows.
Can one estimate cover several buildings?

Yes. Owners and property managers with more than one Milford building can have one plan, one estimate and one point of contact for the season. The estimate spells out what gets lit at each address and how in-season service works.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Lighting in Milford, MI | Holiday Light Service
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Milford permanent lighting: an app-controlled roofline outline that stays up all year, fitted to historic gables, brackets and long eaves. Free estimates.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: App-controlled roofline lighting that stays up all year, planned around the gables, brackets and long eaves of your house, in the village or the township.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Permanent lighting is a roofline outline that goes up once and stays. A discreet track runs under the eaves, and an app on your phone decides what it shows: a Christmas scene in December, a favorite color for a birthday, or a single warm white line on an ordinary weeknight. In Milford, the house itself sets the plan. Houses in the North Milford Village Historic District include Craftsman and Bungalow designs, whose long, low eaves suit an easy continuous run. A Queen Anne or Italianate asks more of the layout around gables, brackets and corners, so we measure every one before the estimate goes out.
considerations: Every corner is a place where an outline can break. On older homes with cross gables or bracketed eaves, we work out where the line turns, where it pauses and how it clears each bracket, so the roofline reads as one clean line at night rather than a string of pieces.

Homes in the North Milford Village Historic District, and homes in a subdivision with an association, may face rules about permanent fixtures on the outside of the house. Find out before you sign. The written estimate lists the layout and mounting hardware, the details a village office or an association board would ask to see.

On a Queen Anne or a Bungalow, the porch roof is often the line people see first from the sidewalk. Adding it to the plan frames the front door and carries the outline down toward the street. We mark it as its own section at the estimate, so you can weigh what it adds before you decide.
faq: Does permanent lighting work on an older Milford home?

Often, yes, with careful planning. The track mounts under the eaves, so it follows the roofline rather than covering the facade. Gables, brackets and decorative trim take extra measuring, and the estimate shows exactly where each run goes.
Can I use the lights outside the holidays?

That is the point. Keep a warm white outline for ordinary evenings, pick a color for a birthday or a graduation, and switch to a full Christmas scene in time for downtown's Christmas Parade, all from the app on your phone.
Is permanent lighting available in Milford Township too?

Yes. The village and the township are both within our service area. Send your address through the request form or call (248) 756-8915, and we will measure your roofline and send a free estimate that spells out what is included.
